rationale: I read the complete held EO 8706 (6 FR 1333, Mar. 8, 1941, signed Mar. 6, 1941): a one-paragraph order amending paragraph 12 only of EO 5865 of June 27, 1932 (regulations on aerial flights by Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard and National Guard personnel) by restating the suspension-from-flying rule; it has no own term and no savings clause, so its operative effect exists only as text of EO 5865. I read the held full text of EO 9195 (7 FR 5257, July 10, 1942, signed July 7, 1942), a complete new set of aerial-flight regulations (paragraphs 1-14, including paragraph 12, its own restatement of the suspension-from-flying rule, extended to nurses). Paragraph 14 closes with: 'the provisions of this order shall be effective as of June 1, 1942, and shall supersede Executive Order No. 5865 of June 27, 1932, as amended by Executive Order No. 8706 of March 6, 1941' (paragraph 10(f) effective from Dec. 7, 1941). That names EO 8706 by number together with its base order and replaces the whole subject. D6 self-check: the only history events are the OFR note 'Amends: EO 5865' and 'Superseded by: EO 9195, July 6, 1942' (the catalog date differs from the held signing date of July 7, 1942; the held text controls). I looked for later events that revive, extend or re-delegate paragraph 12 of EO 5865 or EO 8706: a scan of the held full-run texts finds the number 5865 only as page-number or hash noise outside EO 9195 and EO 8706, and no held order mentions 8706. The 1989 snapshot row is empty and the editorial bound is a lead only. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (June 1, 1942) is not otherwise adjudicated.
